title: Phenoscape: Identifying Candidate Genes for Evolutionary Phenotypes
what_it_did: Used the Phenoscape KB to find zebrafish (ZFIN) mutant phenotypes matching ancestral catfish phenotypes (loss of basihyal, loss of scales), then tested candidate genes (brpf1, eda/edar) by in situ expression in channel catfish.
relation_to_delphi: part (closest family): ontology-linked evolutionary phenotype -> model-organism gene -> expression test in a non-model fish

title: Phenoscape: Semantic analysis of organismal traits and genes yields insights in evolutionary biology
what_it_did: Preprint overview of Phenoscape: semantic annotation tools and the Phenoscape KB, which uses machine (OWL) reasoning to connect evolutionary phenotypes from comparative literature to model-organism mutant phenotypes; candidate-gene linking and synthetic character matrices.
relation_to_delphi: part (closest): ontology-linked evolutionary phenotypes + genes across taxa; OWL reasoning, not proof-assistant verification

title: 500,000 fish phenotypes: The new informatics landscape for evolutionary and developmental biology of the vertebrate skeleton
what_it_did: Built the Phenoscape KB with a community fish anatomy ontology and EQ annotation of about 500,000 fish phenotypes from the comparative literature, linked to ZFIN zebrafish genetic data to yield candidate genes for skeletal evolution.

title: Toward Synthesizing Our Knowledge of Morphology: Using Ontologies and Machine Reasoning to Extract Presence/Absence Evolutionary Phenotypes across Studies
what_it_did: Used ontology reasoning over the Phenoscape KB (55+ sarcopterygian studies) to build a synthetic presence/absence supermatrix (639 characters x 1051 taxa); reasoning detected conflicts and identified undersampled character space across the fin-to-limb transition.
relation_to_delphi: part: the fin-to-limb transition already treated computationally with Uberon-based reasoning (automated DL reasoning, not a proof assistant)

title: A Logical Model of Homology for Comparative Biology
what_it_did: Compared two OWL logical models of homology (REA, AVA) on homology assertions and taxon phenotypes for skeletal elements of vertebrate fins and limbs from the Phenoscape KB, using seven competency questions; reported limits of OWL reasoning.
relation_to_delphi: part: formal (OWL) logic over fin/limb anatomy; closest to our formal-verification layer, but description logic plus reasoner, not a proof assistant

title: Automated Integration of Trees and Traits: A Case Study Using Paired Fin Loss Across Teleost Fishes
what_it_did: Pipeline integrating Phenoscape KB pectoral/pelvic fin presence/absence data with a 12,582-species teleost phylogeny to study paired-fin loss.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: ontology fin traits at clade scale (fin loss, not fin enlargement)

title: An ontological morphological phylogenetic framework for living and extinct ray‐finned fishes (Actinopterygii)
what_it_did: Built an ontological morphological phylogenetic framework for living and extinct ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii).

title: Phenex: Ontological Annotation of Phenotypic Diversity
what_it_did: Phenex: desktop tool for Entity-Quality annotation of evolutionary character data with anatomy, quality (PATO) and taxonomy ontologies.

title: The Teleost Anatomy Ontology: Anatomical Representation for the Genomics Age
what_it_did: Teleost Anatomy Ontology: multispecies fish anatomy ontology built for the Phenoscape evolutionary-morphology database mapping to genetic databases.
relation_to_delphi: part: fish anatomy hierarchy (later merged into Uberon)

title: Connecting evolutionary morphology to genomics using ontologies: a case study from Cypriniformes including zebrafish
what_it_did: Early Phenoscape-precursor paper proposing to connect Cypriniformes evolutionary anatomy to ZFIN via ontologies.

title: Linking Human Diseases to Animal Models Using Ontology-Based Phenotype Annotation
what_it_did: EQ ontology annotation of 11 human gene-linked diseases and comparison with model-organism mutant phenotypes to discover genotype-phenotype relationships across species.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: cross-species G2P via ontologies (human disease)

title: Uberon, an integrative multi-species anatomy ontology
what_it_did: Uberon: species-neutral integrated anatomy ontology (over 6,500 classes at publication) with links to species ontologies and representation of taxonomic variation.
relation_to_delphi: we reuse it (anatomy backbone); must cite

title: Unification of multi-species vertebrate anatomy ontologies for comparative biology in Uberon
what_it_did: Unified multi-species vertebrate anatomy ontologies (including fish, Phenoscape-derived) into Uberon for comparative biology.

title: Logical Development of the Cell Ontology
what_it_did: Computable genus-differentia definitions for over 340 Cell Ontology classes; automated reasoners used to verify the ontology and reveal manual errors.
relation_to_delphi: part: automated (DL reasoner) verification of a biological ontology; prior art for 'verifying' ontology structure

title: The Cell Ontology in the age of single-cell omics
what_it_did: Describes Cell Ontology uses and extensions for single-cell omics atlases.

title: The zebrafish anatomy and stage ontologies: representing the anatomy and development of Danio rerio
what_it_did: Zebrafish anatomy (ZFA) and stage (ZFS) ontologies with subclass, partonomy and developmental hierarchies; used by ZFIN to annotate expression and phenotype.
relation_to_delphi: part: a fish body-to-cell partonomy already used to anchor expression and phenotype data

title: A reference ontology for biomedical informatics: the Foundational Model of Anatomy
what_it_did: Foundational Model of Anatomy: reference ontology of human body structure from molecular to macroscopic levels.
relation_to_delphi: part: a body-to-molecule structural hierarchy (human only, no expression or G2P)

title: Anatomical structures, cell types and biomarkers of the Human Reference Atlas
what_it_did: Perspective presenting Human Reference Atlas 3D anatomy linked to ASCT+B tables that name and interlink anatomical structures, cell types and biomarkers (16 consortia).
relation_to_delphi: part (closest for the layered hierarchy-plus-genes idea): organ -> structure -> cell type -> marker genes with Uberon/CL; human, no evolution, no proofs

title: Construction, Deployment, and Usage of the Human Reference Atlas Knowledge Graph
what_it_did: HRA Knowledge Graph v2.2 (May 2025): 71 organs, 5,800 anatomical structures, 2,268 cell types, 2,531 biomarkers as RDF/SPARQL.
relation_to_delphi: part: the largest built ontology-linked body -> cell -> biomarker graph we found

title: Functional tissue units in the Human Reference Atlas
what_it_did: Catalog of 22 nested functional tissue units in 10 human organs, mapped to Uberon and CL, with dimensions and cell composition.

title: The Bgee suite: integrated curated expression atlas and comparative transcriptomics in animals
what_it_did: Bgee: curated healthy wild-type expression atlas across animal species, anatomy-annotated and comparable across species.
relation_to_delphi: part: the expression-at-anatomy layer; a source we could use

title: Bgee in 2024: focus on curated single-cell RNA-seq datasets, and query tools
what_it_did: Bgee 2024: curated single-cell RNA-seq integrated; expression to cell resolution comparable across species.

title: vHOG, a multispecies vertebrate ontology of homologous organs groups
what_it_did: vHOG: vertebrate homologous-organ-groups ontology used by Bgee to compare expression between species.

title: Zebrafish information network, the knowledgebase for Danio rerio research
what_it_did: ZFIN: zebrafish knowledgebase of genes, alleles, expression and phenotype annotated to anatomy ontologies.
relation_to_delphi: part: source of expression and G2P at anatomical terms for teleosts

title: The Monarch Initiative: an integrative data and analytic platform connecting phenotypes to genotypes across species
what_it_did: Monarch Initiative: ontology-based integration of genes, variants, genotypes, phenotypes and diseases across species.
relation_to_delphi: part: cross-species G2P with ontologies (biomedical focus)

title: The Monarch Initiative in 2024: an analytic platform integrating phenotypes, genes and diseases across species
what_it_did: Monarch 2024: cloud knowledge-graph platform integrating phenotypes, genes and diseases across species.

title: The Unified Phenotype Ontology : a framework for cross-species integrative phenomics
what_it_did: Unified Phenotype Ontology (uPheno) for cross-species integrative phenomics.

title: A Whole-Cell Computational Model Predicts Phenotype from Genotype
what_it_did: Whole-cell model of the M. genitalium life cycle covering all annotated gene functions; validated against diverse data; predicts phenotype from genotype.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: genotype -> phenotype simulation, single cell, no anatomy ontology, no proofs

title: The principles of whole-cell modeling.
what_it_did: States principles of whole-cell modeling, including functional, genetic, molecular and temporal completeness.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: an explicit 'completeness' vocabulary (dimensions, not ordered levels); relevant to our levels 0-5

title: Designing minimal genomes using whole-cell models
what_it_did: Design-simulate-test cycles on the M. genitalium whole-cell model to design in silico minimal genomes.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: computational genome design driven by a whole-cell model

title: Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome
what_it_did: Designed and chemically synthesized JCVI-syn3.0 (531 kbp, 473 genes) by design-build-test cycles; 149 genes of unknown function.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: an organism actually designed and built (cell level)

title: Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0, an engineered derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides , encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors
what_it_did: Analyzed the 50-60 JCVI-syn3.0 proteins still lacking function a decade later using sequence, conservation and AlphaFold models.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: limits of knowing even a minimal organism's parts

title: How to build the virtual cell with artificial intelligence: Priorities and opportunities
what_it_did: Perspective proposing an AI virtual cell (multi-scale, multi-modal neural model of molecules, cells, tissues).

title: Virtual Cell Challenge: Toward a Turing test for the virtual cell
what_it_did: Announces the Arc Institute Virtual Cell Challenge, a recurring benchmark for predicting cellular responses to perturbations.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: evaluation framework for virtual cells

title: Computational physiology and the physiome project
what_it_did: Physiome Project review: physics-based models on anatomical geometry linking proteins to cells, tissues, organs and organ systems (e.g., ion-channel genotype to ECG).
relation_to_delphi: part: multiscale body-to-molecule modelling (quantitative physiology, human)

title: Bioinformatics, multiscale modeling and the IUPS Physiome Project
what_it_did: Physiome: multiscale modeling and markup languages (CellML) linking organ/tissue to subcellular processes; heart Physiome.

title: The VPH-Physiome Project: Standards and Tools for Multiscale Modeling in Clinical Applications
what_it_did: VPH-Physiome Project standards, tools and databases for multiscale modeling in clinical applications.

title: The Physiome Project and Digital Twins
what_it_did: Argues for a physics-constrained virtual human with a comprehensive knowledge graph of all human anatomy and physiology, multiscale down to protein function; reviews progress toward it.
relation_to_delphi: part (vision plus progress): nearest stated goal to a full body -> molecule organism model, but human and physics-based

title: Ontology of physics for biology: representing physical dependencies as a basis for biological processes
what_it_did: Ontology of Physics for Biology: physical-dependency classes for annotating physiome models.

title: OpenWorm: an open-science approach to modeling Caenorhabditis elegans
what_it_did: OpenWorm: open collaboration and modular simulation engine for C. elegans (neuronal plus soft-body physics).
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: a 'digital organism', simulation-first, not ontology/G2P-first

title: An integrative data-driven model simulating C. elegans brain, body and environment interactions
what_it_did: MetaWorm: integrated data-driven C. elegans brain + body + environment model reproducing locomotion.

title: Fossils, genes and the evolution of animal limbs
what_it_did: Review: appendage evolution (fins, limbs, insect wings) correlated with regulatory changes in patterning genes; similar genetic regulatory system across phyla.
relation_to_delphi: background: deep homology of appendages; cite for fin-to-limb/wing framing

title: The fin-to-limb transition as the re-organization of a Turing pattern
what_it_did: Catshark fin skeletal patterning explained by a conserved Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network; model predictions matched perturbation experiments.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: mechanistic regulation -> form model for fin-to-limb

title: A computational model of teeth and the developmental origins of morphological variation
what_it_did: Computational model of mammalian tooth development combining genetic and cellular interaction parameters to generate 3D teeth; mapped parameters to population variation in seals.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: generates organ form from developmental genetics (our levels 3-4 at organ scale)

title: LimbNET: collaborative platform for simulating spatial patterns of gene networks in limb development
what_it_did: LimbNET: web platform to define and simulate GRN models of 2D limb patterning mapped to image-derived expression.

title: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes
what_it_did: Phylogenomics of 35 flying fish species and relatives found coding/regulatory signatures of convergent paired-fin enlargement; intersected with zebrafish fin-size mutants; lat4a and kcnh2a interaction phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions in zebrafish.
relation_to_delphi: key empirical source for the worked case; must cite

title: longfin causes cis -ectopic expression of the kcnh2a ether-a-go-go K+ channel to autonomously prolong fin outgrowth
what_it_did: Zebrafish longfin t2 is a cis-regulatory allele causing ectopic kcnh2a expression that prolongs fin outgrowth tissue-autonomously.

title: Molecular systematics of flyingfishes (Teleostei: Exocoetidae): evolution in the epipelagic zone
what_it_did: Species-level molecular phylogeny of Exocoetidae (cyt b, RAG2) and evolution of gliding traits.

title: K-Lean: Machine-Verified Formal Proofs for Computational Biology
what_it_did: K-Lean (preprint, 2026): Lean 4 library of 94 formal contracts for computational-biology quantities (kinetics, structure metrics, etc.).
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: Lean in computational biology, but numeric/algorithmic properties, not anatomy hierarchies

title: Formalizing chemical physics using the Lean theorem prover
what_it_did: Formalized chemical physics theories in Lean.

title: Reasoning about the Genetic Code in Lean
what_it_did: Lean 4 model of the central dogma: proves redundancy of the genetic code, injectivity of transcription, non-injectivity of translation (arXiv, Oct 2026).
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: proof assistant over a genotype -> product map, molecular only

title: Temporal logic patterns for querying dynamic models of cellular interaction networks
what_it_did: Temporal-logic query patterns for model checking dynamic models of cellular interaction networks (E. coli carbon starvation).
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: formal verification of regulatory dynamics (our level 3)

title: Modelling and Verifying Dynamic Properties of Neuronal Networks in Coq
what_it_did: Thesis: modelled basic neuronal circuits in Coq and proved dynamic properties.

title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
what_it_did: AI evolutionary search designed candidate reconfigurable organisms in silico; designs built from frog cells with the predicted behaviours.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: an actual 'generate an organism' pipeline, but from cells and physics, not ontology plus genes

title: Sequence modeling and design from molecular to genome scale with Evo
what_it_did: Evo: 7B-parameter genomic foundation model for prediction and generation from molecular to genome scale (prokaryotes).

title: Genome modelling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2
what_it_did: Evo 2: genomic model trained on 9T bp across all domains of life; variant-effect prediction and design.

title: Generative design of novel bacteriophages with genome language models
what_it_did: Generated whole bacteriophage genomes with Evo 1/2; 16 viable phages experimentally confirmed.
relation_to_delphi: adjacent: first verified generated whole genomes (viruses)

title: The Genomic Code: the genome instantiates a generative model of the organism
what_it_did: Theory paper proposing the genome encodes a generative model (VAE analogy) of the organism, decoded through development.
